questions.prompt: In a fair test, the one factor a scientist deliberately changes to see its effect is called the:
questions.explanation: The factor the scientist deliberately changes is the variable being tested; everything else should be kept the same to make the test fair.

questions.prompt: Which everyday activity in Ethiopia depends most directly on knowledge from biology?
options: Growing healthier teff and treating crop diseases
Measuring the speed of a car
questions.explanation: Improving crops and controlling plant diseases depends on biology, the study of living things. The other tasks rely mainly on geology, physics, or chemistry.

questions.prompt: Which part of the cell is the jelly-like substance where many chemical reactions take place?
questions.explanation: The cytoplasm is the jelly-like material that fills the cell and is where many of the cell's chemical reactions happen.

questions.prompt: Which fluid is released in the mouth to begin softening food and starting the digestion of starch?
questions.explanation: Saliva moistens the food and contains an enzyme that begins breaking down starch in the mouth.

questions.prompt: Mould growing on old bread is an example of which type of micro-organism?
questions.explanation: Mould is a type of fungus. It grows on food such as bread and feeds on it, often spoiling it.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a non-living (abiotic) part of an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Sunlight is a non-living (abiotic) factor. The grasshopper, tree, and bird are all living (biotic) parts of the ecosystem.

questions.prompt: After collecting and studying the results of an experiment, the statement a scientist writes about what the results show is called the:
questions.explanation: A conclusion is the statement that explains what the results mean and whether they support the hypothesis.

questions.prompt: Why is conserving many different local varieties of a crop, as done in Ethiopian seed banks, useful for farmers?
options: Different varieties may survive drought, pests, or disease when others fail
It removes the need to plant seeds
questions.explanation: Keeping a wide variety of seeds means that if one type is wiped out by drought or disease, other varieties with different strengths may survive, protecting the food supply.

questions.prompt: A root hair cell has a long, thin extension. How does this shape help the plant?
options: It increases the surface area for absorbing water and minerals
questions.explanation: The long extension of a root hair cell increases its surface area, allowing the plant to absorb more water and dissolved minerals from the soil.

questions.prompt: What is the main job of the large central vacuole in a plant cell?
options: To store cell sap and help keep the cell firm
questions.explanation: The large vacuole stores cell sap, and when full of liquid it presses outward and helps keep the plant cell firm (turgid).

questions.prompt: Besides giving energy, what is another important role of fats in the human body?
options: Storing energy and helping to keep the body warm
questions.explanation: Fats store energy for later use and form a layer under the skin that helps insulate the body and keep it warm.

questions.prompt: Which blood cells help to defend the body by fighting germs?
questions.explanation: White blood cells are part of the immune system and help defend the body by attacking and destroying germs.

questions.prompt: Why does keeping food in a cool place, such as a refrigerator, help it last longer?
options: Cold slows down the growth of micro-organisms that spoil food
questions.explanation: Most micro-organisms grow slowly in the cold, so keeping food cool slows the spoiling caused by bacteria and fungi.

questions.prompt: Tuberculosis (TB) can spread when an infected person coughs. This is an example of a disease spread mainly by:
options: The air (droplets from coughs and sneezes)
questions.explanation: TB bacteria can travel in tiny droplets released when an infected person coughs or sneezes, so it spreads mainly through the air.

questions.topic: Why one common name is a problem
questions.prompt: Why can using only local common names for an organism cause confusion between scientists in different regions?
options: Common names are too long to say
The same organism may have many different local names, or one name may be used for different organisms
Common names are always in Latin
questions.explanation: The same organism can have many different local names, and the same name can be used for different organisms, so a single agreed scientific name avoids the confusion.

questions.prompt: An Amoeba is a single-celled organism with a true nucleus that lives in water. To which kingdom does it belong?
questions.explanation: Amoeba is a mostly single-celled organism with a true nucleus, which places it in the kingdom Protista.

questions.prompt: All the zebras living together in one area at the same time are best described as a:
questions.explanation: A population is all the members of the same species living in the same area at the same time, such as all the zebras in one area.

questions.prompt: When yeast is added to dough, the dough rises. Which gas produced by the yeast makes the dough rise?
questions.explanation: As yeast breaks down sugars it releases carbon dioxide gas, and the bubbles of this gas make the dough rise.

questions.prompt: A scientist tests a new plant medicine on only three people and it seems to work. Why should other scientists be careful before accepting it?
options: Three people is too few to be sure the result is reliable
questions.explanation: A result from only a few people may happen by chance. The work must be repeated on many people and checked by others before it can be trusted.

questions.prompt: A drop of dye spreads faster in hot water than in cold water. Why does a higher temperature increase the rate of diffusion?
options: The particles have more energy and move faster
questions.explanation: At higher temperatures particles have more energy and move faster, so they spread out (diffuse) more quickly.

questions.prompt: A piece of fresh potato is placed in pure water. What is most likely to happen to the potato cells?
options: They gain water by osmosis and become firmer
questions.explanation: Pure water has a higher water concentration than the potato cells, so water moves into the cells by osmosis, making them swollen and firm.

questions.prompt: The stomach produces acid during digestion. Apart from helping enzymes work, what other useful job does this acid do?
options: It adds oxygen to the blood
It kills many germs that are swallowed with food
questions.explanation: Stomach acid creates conditions that help digestive enzymes act on protein and also kills many of the germs that enter with food.

questions.prompt: Capillaries have very thin walls, only one cell thick. How does this help the body?
options: It lets oxygen and food pass easily between blood and the cells
questions.explanation: The very thin walls of capillaries allow oxygen, food, and waste substances to pass quickly between the blood and the surrounding body cells.

questions.prompt: How does unbroken skin help protect the body against disease?
options: It forms a barrier that stops many germs from entering the body
questions.explanation: Unbroken skin acts as a physical barrier that keeps many germs out. Germs find it easier to enter through cuts or wounds.

questions.prompt: Scientists often identify an unknown organism using a tool that asks a series of paired yes/no questions about its features. This tool is called a:
questions.explanation: A classification or identification key uses a series of paired questions about features to guide the user step by step to the name of the organism.

questions.prompt: If two organisms are placed in the same small group during classification, what does this usually suggest?
options: One must be a plant and one an animal
They share many features and are closely related
questions.explanation: Organisms grouped closely together share many features, which usually means they are closely related to each other.

questions.prompt: In an area, the number of rats (prey) rises sharply. What is most likely to happen to the number of snakes (predators) that eat them?
options: The snakes will decrease because there is more food
The snakes will increase because there is more food
The snakes will turn into rats
questions.explanation: With more prey available, more snakes can find food and survive, so the predator population is likely to increase.

questions.prompt: Which process removes carbon dioxide from the air and helps balance the gas given out by respiration and burning?
questions.explanation: Green plants take in carbon dioxide during photosynthesis, which helps balance the carbon dioxide released by respiration and the burning of fuels.

questions.prompt: Which group is LARGER and contains more kinds of organisms?
questions.explanation: A genus is a larger group that can contain several closely related species, so it includes more kinds of organisms than a single species.

questions.prompt: A student wants to look at the colour and shape of a living water flea while it is still moving. Which instrument is the BEST choice?
options: An electron microscope, because it kills the specimen
A light microscope, because it can view living specimens
A telescope, because the flea is far away
A weighing balance, because it shows colour
questions.explanation: A light microscope can be used on living, moving specimens, while an electron microscope only works on dead material in a vacuum.

questions.prompt: Very small cells exchange substances with their surroundings more efficiently than very large cells mainly because small cells have:
options: A larger surface area compared with their volume
questions.explanation: Small cells have a larger surface area relative to their volume, so substances can diffuse in and out fast enough to supply the whole cell.

questions.prompt: When a person runs hard, their breathing rate increases. What is the MAIN reason for this?
options: To supply more oxygen and remove more carbon dioxide for faster respiration
questions.explanation: Exercising muscles respire faster and need more oxygen and produce more carbon dioxide, so breathing speeds up to supply the oxygen and remove the carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: A person whose diet lacks iron may feel tired and weak. This is most directly because the body cannot make enough:
options: Healthy red blood cells to carry oxygen
questions.explanation: Iron is needed to make red blood cells that carry oxygen. Without enough iron the blood carries less oxygen, leaving the person tired and weak (anaemia).

questions.prompt: Which statement about a person living with HIV is correct?
options: You can catch HIV by sitting next to them in class
Their cough spreads HIV through the air
Touching their hand will infect you
They can live and work normally, and sharing food or hugging is safe
questions.explanation: HIV is not spread by everyday contact such as sitting together, sharing food, hugging, or shaking hands, so a person with HIV can study and work normally.

questions.prompt: A learner observes two microbes: one is single-celled with no true nucleus, the other is a thread-like mould feeding on dead matter. Into which kingdoms do they belong, in order?
questions.explanation: A single-celled microbe with no true nucleus is in Monera (bacteria), while a thread-like mould that feeds on dead matter is a fungus, in the Fungi kingdom.

questions.prompt: Some animals in hot Ethiopian lowlands rest in shade during the hottest part of the day and feed in the cool evening. This behaviour is an adaptation because it:
options: Helps them avoid extreme heat and save water
Helps them make their own food
Stops them from ever needing food
questions.explanation: Resting in shade during the heat and being active when it is cooler helps the animals avoid overheating and lose less water, improving their chance of survival.
